Recent research supports separating topical relevance from usefulness for a user’s current decision. A SIGIR 2024 study found that including follow-up feedback clarified this distinction and improved annotator agreement for ambiguous requests ([Siro et al.](https://irlab.science.uva.nl/wp-content/papercite-data/pdf/siro-2024-rethinking.pdf)). The 2025 ALERT benchmark reports 70% concordance with expert judgments when evaluating recommendation explanations—evidence that automated judgments still require calibration, rather than establishing users’ actual intent ([ALERT](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.137/)).

Proposed annotation protocol: retain separate fields for relevance, immediate intent, rejection and identity certainty. “Choose-now” requires explicit willingness to select the item now; “generally relevant” requires supported interest without immediate commitment; “explicit rejection” requires a negative statement; “uncertain identity” flags unresolved product, edition or variant identification. Allow unknown values and overlapping fields: a relevant item can still be rejected. Store user/category/item identifiers, rank, verbatim feedback, evidence spans and annotation rationale. Distinguish real-user statements from simulator-generated feedback. Record redundancy only with an identifiable duplicate or substantive overlap; assess compatibility only against explicit specifications in available histories, titles or descriptions. History alone does not establish ownership, mood or current need.

For twenty users, five per category, independently double-code all reviewed recommendations using a frozen codebook. Report pre-adjudication raw agreement, nominal Krippendorff’s alpha per field, confusion tables and adjudicated counts. Give numerator/denominator, distinct-user support and unknown counts for every finding; compatibility rates require an assessable-case denominator. Preserve original disagreements and document resolutions. These are proposed audit procedures, not measured results. Keep this small-sample feedback diagnostic separate from official selection, which remains macro-average validation HR@10.
